title: fix(lint): skill tool references stay a whole-stack verdict; the runtime door never judges them
body:
Fixes #19527

Clause-②: no

This carries out ruling `5791822697` on #19527 (batch 215 item 4, letter B, maintainer 「215 同意」): 「cross-item reference resolution belongs to the whole-stack rule」. `ai-skill-tool-unresolved` is reported by `os validate` / `os lint` / `os build`. The runtime publish door never emits it. `RuntimeStackContext` and `CONTEXT_STACK_KEYS` are unchanged (ruling item 3), and no rule was added (item 2).

## What was measured first, on `origin/main` @ `1f89ba0d70` (before any edit)

The measurement ran from a scratch `tsx` script against `packages/lint/src`. I deleted the script afterwards and did not commit it.

| probe | reading |
|---|---|
| `runtimeGatedTypes()` | 17 types: `action app book dashboard dataset datasource email_template flow hook mapping object page permission position report seed view`. **`skill` is not one of them** |
| `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor('skill')` / `stackKeyForType('skill')` | `[]` / `null` |
| the wiring guard's unmapped set, `runtimeGatedTypes().filter(t => stackKeyForType(t) === null)` | `[]` |
| the real door, a `skill` write naming a stack-level action / a plugin tool / a tool that exists nowhere | `errors: [] · advisories: [] · rulesRun: []` for all three |
| the card's reproduction: `validateAiToolReferences` on the door's snapshot shape (`objects permissions books datasets`, with `actions` dropped by the builder) | `ai-skill-tool-unresolved` for all three |
| the same member over the whole stack (with `stack.actions`) | stack-level action: `[]` · plugin tool: `ai-skill-tool-unresolved` · missing tool: `ai-skill-tool-unresolved` |
| a `flow` write, which dispatches the suite with this member on its frozen `flow` default | 0 `ai-skill-tool-unresolved`: no door snapshot carries `skills` (`WRITTEN_STACK_KEYS` has no `skills`) |

⚠️ **The door does not emit the false advisory on `main` today.** `skill` has been outside the door since #19542, and the card says so itself ("Nothing is broken today"). The advisory appears only if the type is crossed. The reproduction is the rule run on the door's snapshot shape (the LIT case), and ablation 1 below produces it through the real door. So this PR changes no runtime behaviour. It turns a hold-out that was waiting on a wider snapshot into a design boundary, and it pins both halves of the ruling. I re-ran the measurement script after the edits and its output was byte-identical to the base run.

## Which of the two shapes the wiring guard allows: `skill` stays OUTSIDE the door

The guard (`authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts`, 「every runtime-gated metadata type maps to a stack key」) checks `runtimeGatedTypes()`. That set is built from rule `runtimeTypes` declarations, not listed by hand. `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` returns `empty` at `rules.length === 0`, before it looks at `TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY`. So a type with an empty runtime rule set is not a gated type, and "crossed with an empty rule set" can only be written in two ways:

- declare `skill` on some entry (for example the reference-integrity suite) with no member claiming it. Then `rulesRun` names a rule that judges nothing, which is the ruling's ⛔ on inventing a rule to give the door something to run.
- add a `skill: 'skills'` row with no rule declaring it. The gate never reads such a row, which is the mapping-ahead-of-its-rules shape `runtime-gate.ts` refuses (the `seed: 'data'` note).

So both absences stay, and the guard holds with `skill` outside it.

## The change

Comments are restated from 「held out on a measurement」 to 「by design: cross-item reference resolution belongs to the whole-stack rule」, citing the ruling. Each place also drops the old "cross it once `actions` / `tools` are carried" direction, which the ruling rejected:

- `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`, the `skill` block on the `validateReferenceIntegrity` entry.
- `packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts`, the `validateAiToolReferences` member. This member held the measurement and still prescribed widening the snapshot. It now cites ADR-0109 Decision §3 as the governing text.
- `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts`, the `skill` note on `TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY`.
- `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.inert-type-writes.test.ts`: the file header, the `GROUP_A` docblock, the `skill` block and the report/skill fence comment. The two DARK pins keep their assertions, and their reason text now points at the ruling.
- `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.datasource-writes.test.ts`: two comments that call `skill` "held out on the measurement". This is the second place that pins both halves (`runtimeAuthoringRulesFor('skill')` is `[]` and `stackKeyForType('skill')` is null).

The LIT case 「one skill, one rule, two universes」 stays as the reason pin. Its snapshot-bound assertion now says what a red means under the ruling: someone widened `RuntimeStackContext` against item 3. It no longer says `skill` may now cross.

New cases in the `skill` block of `runtime-gate.inert-type-writes.test.ts`:

- **(a)** `it.each` over three tools (a stack-level AI-exposed action, a plugin-registered tool, a tool that exists nowhere). A `skill` write through the real door returns `errors []`, `advisories []` and `rulesRun []`. The in-process firing control: the member the door does not dispatch **does** return `ai-skill-tool-unresolved` on the door's snapshot shape for each of the three.
- **(a)** No write type can carry a skill into a door snapshot. No gated type maps to `skills`, and `skills` is not a context key.
- **(b)** `runAuthoringRules` for each of `validate`, `build` and `lint` over a whole stack reports exactly `[{ path: 'skills[1].tools[0]', severity: 'warning' }]`: the tool that exists nowhere is reported, and the stack-level action is not.
- **(c)** The guard invariant holds over the real tables, and a `skill` write's `rulesRun` is `[]`.

## Firing controls: ablations on the committed tree (`eb4f0cae09`)

Each mutation went through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. The tool checked the anchor count and blob hash on disk after each write, and each restore was confirmed as `blob == HEAD` with an empty `git diff HEAD`. No build step was involved: every subject is a relative import inside `packages/lint`, so vitest reads `src`.

| # | mutation | red | green |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | cross `skill` fully: suite entry `runtimeTypes` + member `runtimeTypes: ['flow','skill']` + `skill: 'skills'` row | 9: all three (a) cases, the (a) no-other-write case, (c), both DARK pins, the report/skill fence, and the datasource DARK pin. The (a) failure is the exact false advisory through the real door: `advisories: [{ rule: 'ai-skill-tool-unresolved', path: 'skills[0].tools[0]' }]` for `action_showcase_portfolio_snapshot` | 68, including the wiring guard (a full crossing is consistent) |
| 2 | declare `skill` on the suite entry only | 3: the repo's own 「every runtime-gated metadata type maps to a stack key」, (c), DARK | 64 |
| 3 | delete the `validateAiToolReferences` member | (b): `os validate must still report the tool that exists nowhere: expected [] …` | none (run with `-t`, only (b) selected) |
| 4 | drop `addActionFamily(stack.actions)` from `collectToolUniverse` | (b) gets 2 findings instead of 1, and the LIT lit-control leg fails | none (run with `-t`, only (b) and LIT selected) |

The first attempt at ablation 1 did nothing: its third anchor was a substring of its own replacement, `ablation-replace` refused with "anchor count moved 1 -> 1", and no test ran. All three files were confirmed restored. It was re-run with a non-overlapping multi-line anchor, and those are the readings above.

## Downstream readers of `ai-skill-tool-unresolved`

I ran `git grep` over `packages/`, `skills/`, `content/`, `examples/` and `apps/`. None of these expects the runtime door to emit the rule id, so none needed updating: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx:166`, `content/docs/ai/tools.mdx:92`, `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts:394`, `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts:373`, `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:85`, `packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts:17`, `packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.test.ts:362` and `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.test.ts`. Each one describes a whole-stack (`os validate`) verdict, which is the ruled state. The only door-facing readers were the lint tests edited above. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (`runtime-authoring-gate.ts`, the only source file that imports `@objectstack/lint/runtime`) has no `skill`-specific door logic.

## Changeset: `@objectstack/lint` patch

The dispatch assumed this changes runtime behaviour. The measurement shows it does not (see above). The repo rule still asks for a changeset, because the published bytes change. `@objectstack/lint` ships `dist`, and its build keeps source comments: after the rebuild, the ruling id is in `dist/index.js`, `dist/index.cjs`, `dist/runtime.js` and `dist/runtime.cjs` (3 hits each, one per restated block), and 「held out on a measurement」 is in none of them. That phrase was in `authoring-rules.ts` on the base, so it shipped there. Under AGENTS.md, `skip-changeset` is only for a diff that publishes nothing from a released package, so this takes a `patch`. There is precedent for comment-only changes that ship to `dist` (for example `.changeset/15295-serve-observability-mirror-comment.md`).

Clause-② reading: **no**, with no arm. No authorable key or accept set moves in either direction. The door judged no `skill` write before this PR and judges none after it, and the whole-stack verdict is unchanged. It is neither widening nor narrowing.

## Local verification, at HEAD `fd206c3164`

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: **108 files / 4127 tests passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` and `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0. `check:test-typecheck: OK`. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` includes both edited test files.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (the package that wires the runtime gate): **188 files passed, 3 skipped · 2673 tests passed, 19 skipped**.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands`, derived again after the changeset commit: **59 commands**, all run. `--ran` reports: 「59 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 59 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED」. The first pass got exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) from `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure` and `check:type-check-debt`. After a full `turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*'` (72/72 tasks), all three measured green at the same HEAD.
- **Scoping, declared:** the repo-wide `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint` are left to CI (`Test Core` shards, `Lint & Repo Gates`). `origin/main` has moved 4 commits past the base, and none of them touches `packages/lint`, `packages/metadata-protocol` or `packages/spec/src/ai`.

## Acceptance notes

- `validateAiToolReferences` keeps its frozen `flow` default, so it still runs on every `flow` write. It judges nothing there, because a flow snapshot has no `skills`. I considered an explicit empty member `runtimeTypes` to make "never" structural, but did not make that change, since it would change which members run on flow writes and the ruling did not ask for it. The new (a) case pins that "never" holds for every write type.
- The pair card 19477 (written without the sigil on purpose) still answers 404, as the claim comment recorded.
